tables.title: Contrary evidence and what would change the view

rows.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view — paragraph 1
Chart data: revenue and EBITDA — paragraph 1

limitations: Produced in a host session and accepted by the CP-OS check.
Literal checked analytical handoff, not native contract acceptance; source qualifications and gaps remain.

- No financial statements, results or trading update after December 31, 2025 are supplied, so leverage, interest cover, liquidity and every other figure here stop at that date; this restricts every conclusion about the credit today. Severity High. Action: obtain post-closing financial statements or lender reports for the company. - The capital structure after the merger completed on April 9, 2026 is not stated: the debt commitment letter is mentioned without terms, so net debt after closing cannot be stated and year-end net debt of USD 3,665.7 million is the last figure available. Severity High. Action: obtain the financing documents or a post-closing debt schedule. - The outcome for the 1.573% senior secured notes due October 2026 (USD 600 million) and for the USD 600 million delayed draw term loan available to October 15, 2026 is not stated, so year-end current debt and the 2026 maturity cannot be rolled forward. Severity Medium. Action: obtain the debt schedule at a date after October 2026. - Undrawn committed facilities differ across sources for FY2025: USD 1,000 million of revolver in the annual report, about USD 1,060 million of unused committed lines in the results release, and USD 1,197.0 million of unused lines of which the committed share is not split; no letters of credit are stated. This restricts the liquidity chart for FY2025, FY2024 and FY2023. Severity Medium. Action: obtain the committed and uncommitted split by facility. - The covenant leverage definition is not stated: the annual report calls the measure debt to EBITDA in one place and a net leverage ratio in the risk factors, and the covenant EBITDA definition is not given. This restricts any headroom conclusion for FY2025 and FY2024. Severity Medium. Action: obtain the credit agreement. - Maturities after 2030 of USD 1,281.8 million are one total, so the maturity chart stops at 2030, and USD 5.0 million of the difference between scheduled principal and carrying value is not itemized. This restricts the year-by-year wall beyond 2030. Severity Medium. Action: obtain note-level principal and the lease schedule. - Principal is not stated for the 4.000% 2027, 5.000% 2029 and 6.875% 2033 notes, and security and ranking are not described for them (USD 1,293.7 million at carrying value); outstanding principal, drawn amount, margin, floor and reference-rate spread are not stated for the Term Loan A, the revolver or the delayed draw term loan; the rate type is not stated for the notes whose filing gives only a rate. This restricts the debt stack, which omits those notes, and the cumulative leverage of unsecured debt. Severity Medium. Action: obtain the indentures and the credit agreement. - The U.S. securitization program started in December 2025 derecognizes USD 50.0 million of receivables outside debt with cash in operating activities, which makes FY2025 total debt and operating cash flow not fully comparable with FY2024. This restricts year-on-year debt and cash flow comparisons by about USD 50.0 million. Severity Medium. Action: carry the program beside debt in later analysis. - Several cash flow cells are printed as dashes in the filing and are carried as not supplied rather than zero: impairment of debt investment in FY2025 and FY2023, tax refunds and deposits in FY2025, businesses acquired in FY2025, and repurchases of common stock in FY2025 and FY2024. This restricts nothing material because the activity totals tie. Severity Low. Action: none unless a dash is shown to be a nil amount. - The cash flow statement closes on cash, cash equivalents and restricted cash of USD 345.3 million while the balance sheet shows cash of USD 344.0 million, a restricted amount of USD 1.3 million; net debt uses the balance sheet figure. Severity Low. Action: none. - Funds from operations is not stated by the issuer and the method gives no formula, so funds from operations to debt is not calculable for any period. This restricts one coverage measure only. Severity Low. Action: define an agreed funds from operations proxy if committee needs it. - No interim statements are supplied beyond the fourth quarter 2025 three-month columns of the results release, so no last-twelve-months figure is constructed and the quarterly trend is not available. This restricts quarterly leverage analysis only. Severity Low. Action: none while the full-year figures stand. - Interest income is netted within interest expense, net and is stated only inside the interest expense table, so gross interest cost is a calculation (USD 274.8 million for FY2025) and not a reported line. Severity Low. Action: none.

facts.text: - Liquidity is adequate and larger than the earlier financial analysis could show, but it is thin in the United States and sensitive to ratings. facts.text: - Business quality is strong on scale and customer spread, but the Protective segment is eroding and Food carries the credit. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_sealed-air-corp.htm.jsonl, pages 8, 66, 68, 77; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C22; calculation C23; calculation C24; calculation C26; calculation C50

facts.text: - The earnings gains came from cost take-out that has finished, which leaves fewer self-help levers for the next price or volume shock. The restructuring program that concluded in the third quarter of 2025 delivered its full USD 160 million annualized savings target, yet adjusted EBITDA rose only USD 27.7 million between 2023 and 2025 while net sales fell USD 129.1 million, so on a rough comparison about USD 132.3 million of the savings was absorbed by price, volume and other costs. Capital expenditure is planned at USD 225 million for 2026, USD 55.5 million or 32.74% above 2025, which lowers free cash flow by that amount if earnings are unchanged. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_sealed-air-corp.htm.jsonl, pages 61, 70, 82; calculation C18; calculation C19; calculation C20; calculation C44

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: - Refinancing risk is concentrated in 2026 to 2028, and the buyout has turned it from a market-access question into an open one. facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest evidence against a cautious reading is that the filings show a credit that was improving and conservatively run. Debt fell by USD 394.2 million in 2025, the covenant ratio of 2.95x was well inside its 4.50x limit, the revolver was undrawn, bank maturities had been moved to October 2030, and the senior secured debt was rated Baa2 and BBB-, investment grade at both agencies. Protective adjusted EBITDA also rose 21% in the fourth quarter, to USD 80 million from USD 67 million, which suggests the erosion may be bottoming, and management states that U.S. cash and committed facilities available to U.S. borrowers are sufficient for at least the next 12 months. A buyout can also leave existing creditors protected if sponsor equity is large, or end their exposure if the notes were repaid at closing. The view would improve if post-closing statements show leverage on the issuer's own measure no higher than its year-end level, the notes and credit agreement left in place and creditor reporting continuing. It would worsen if the financing adds net debt on a scale where each USD 1,000.0 million adds 0.88x, if the secured layer grows ahead of the unsecured notes, or if Protective volume resumes falling. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_sealed-air-corp.htm.jsonl, pages 58, 82, 84, 85, 86, 150; EX-99.1_2025-12-31_see.htm.jsonl, page 4; calculation C3; calculation C12; calculation C41; calculation C49; calculation C51

facts.label: Company description and ownership
facts.text: Sealed Air Corporation, a Delaware company, is the registrant of a consolidated group that sells packaging materials, automation equipment and services to food processors (Food, 67.1% of 2025 net sales) and to e-commerce, logistics, industrial and medical customers (Protective, 32.9%). Debt service therefore rests on repeat purchasing and the spread of customers rather than contracted backlog, which gives refinancing lenders little revenue visibility beyond the current order flow. The filing describes global and regional competitors competing on performance, automation, sustainability, service and price, with competitors and customers consolidating, and Protective has lost both price and volume since 2023, which is evidence that rivalry caps its pricing; Food, with equipment-integrated materials sold directly to food processors, shows rising margins. facts.label: Competitive forces and external factors
facts.text: The threat of new entrants is moderate, because brands, equipment integration, product registration requirements and plant scale are barriers but the filing says the business does not depend on any single patent or trademark. The threat of substitutes comes from paper, molded pulp and corrugated alternatives in protective packaging and from regulation of plastics and PFAS, which could cut demand or force reformulation; Food's shelf-life and food-safety function makes switching harder, although competing food packaging also uses plastic, metals and other materials. Buyer power is limited by customer spread, with no customer above 10%, but is real in Protective, where distributors carry no minimum purchases, and supplier power is limited because most resins are available from several sources, although sole-source suppliers exist in some regions and a resin spike reaches cost of sales ahead of prices. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_sealed-air-corp.htm.jsonl, pages 9, 13, 14, 15, 16, 25, 36, 37; calculation C50

facts.label: Downside scenario
facts.text: The realistic downside combines a second Protective shock with leverage added by the buyout. The initiating condition is a repeat of 2024, when Protective volume fell USD 101.8 million and price USD 49.3 million, now joined by the weakness already seen in Food's industrial portfolio. The first operational break is distributor and fulfillment volume, which carries no minimum commitments, with price concessions on top; the financial transmission is that a repeat of the 13.35% fall in Protective adjusted EBITDA would cost USD 41.44 million, 3.65% of consolidated adjusted EBITDA, and lower EBITDA cover of cash interest from 3.50x to 3.34x, so the operating shock alone is survivable. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_sealed-air-corp.htm.jsonl, pages 66, 67, 77; calculation C13; calculation C25; calculation C45

facts.label: Downside scenario
facts.text: What would turn it into a liquidity event is the capital structure behind the shock. Each USD 100.0 million of lost reported EBITDA lowers cover of cash interest to 3.12x, each USD 1,000.0 million of acquisition debt adds 0.88x to leverage on adjusted EBITDA, and replacing the October 2026 notes at the 2032 notes' coupon adds USD 29.56 million of interest, while securitization availability shrinks if ratings fall and the revolver is the only large committed source. Management levers are capital expenditure, which fell by USD 74.7 million between 2023 and 2025, the dividend, whose post-closing policy is unknown, and working-capital programs that are already large. Before the buyout resilience was sufficient to avoid liquidity distress, with cover of current debt 1.93x; after it, resilience is not established. The observable triggers are Protective volume, revolver drawings and any amendment or waiver of the credit agreement. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_sealed-air-corp.htm.jsonl, pages 82, 83, 84, 143, 149, 150; calculation C31; calculation C35; calculation C37; calculation C41; calculation C44

facts.label: Overall credit view
facts.text: Overall, Sealed Air presented an adequate business profile at the end of 2025, supported by a USD 5,359.8 million sales base with no customer above 10%, a larger and higher-margin Food segment and conservative pre-sale financial policy, but credit quality is constrained by a Protective segment that lost 17.00% of gross profit in two years, finished cost savings and the loss of visibility after the CD&R buyout. Cash-flow durability appears adequate, because free cash flow was USD 458.5 million and USD 339.3 million after dividends, although up to USD 50.0 million of 2025 operating cash flow came from selling receivables that the old program had carried as debt. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on how the acquisition was financed and whether the October 2026 notes and the bank debt were repaid, amended or waived. The primary downside path is acquisition debt that raises leverage and interest cost while Protective volume stays weak. Further analysis would require the financing documents, a post-closing debt schedule, 2026 interim statements and creditor reporting terms. Fundamental credit assessment completed. Top risk: undisclosed acquisition financing and its effect on leverage, ranking and liquidity. ## Findings
### Bottom line
The four filings support a credit snapshot of Sealed Air as it stood at 2025-12-31, before its acquisition by funds affiliated with CD&R, but they cannot describe its credit today.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_sealed-air-corp.htm.jsonl, pages 7–8; STATUS_15-12G_2026-04-20_see.htm.jsonl, page 1

Creditors should treat every leverage, liquidity and coverage figure drawn from these sources as a pre-transaction picture. The merger completed on April 9, 2026 and the company filed to terminate its public reporting on April 20, 2026, so nothing later is supplied and the as-of date sits 322 days after the last reported balance sheet. The acquisition financing, the outcome for the notes due October 2026 and any rating action after year-end are absent. The 2025 and 2024 annual reports otherwise give Financial foundation, Business & governance and Fundamental credit enough to work on that limited basis.

## Findings
### Bottom line

Sealed Air ended 2025 with net debt of USD 3,665.7 million, or 3.90x reported EBITDA, down from 4.69x two years earlier, but these year-end figures predate the CD&R acquisition and its financing and so do not describe the credit today. Pro forma for the dividend declared on 2026-02-16, net debt is USD 3,695.2 million, or 3.94x.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_sealed-air-corp.htm.jsonl, pages 109, 177; calculation C7; calculation C1; calculation C25; calculation C26

The USD 600 million notes due October 2026 sat in current debt at year-end with their outcome not established, and the sources give no acquisition financing. Cash interest cover was 3.50x, and free cash flow of USD 458.5 million covered dividends of USD 119.2 million. Almost all of the deleveraging came from debt repayment rather than higher earnings.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_sealed-air-corp.htm.jsonl, pages 148–149; calculation C10
### Key findings

- Leverage fell because debt was repaid, not because earnings grew: net debt dropped by USD 678.5 million between 2023 and 2025 while reported EBITDA rose by only USD 12.9 million, taking net leverage from 4.69x to 4.26x and then 3.90x. Total debt over reported EBITDA is still 4.27x, so creditors rely on continued cash generation to keep reducing it.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_sealed-air-corp.htm.jsonl, page 109; 10-K_2024-12-31_sealed-air-corp.htm.jsonl, page 104; calculation C28; calculation C29

- Cash generation funds the repayment: free cash flow after capital expenditure was USD 458.5 million in 2025 and USD 507.8 million in 2024, and after dividends USD 339.3 million and USD 389.8 million. Operating cash flow in 2025 was USD 100.0 million lower than in 2024, a year that included a USD 54.0 million IRS refund.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_sealed-air-corp.htm.jsonl, pages 111–112; calculation C10; calculation C13; calculation C45

- Coverage is moderate: reported EBITDA covered cash interest paid 3.50x in 2025, 3.33x in 2024 and 3.49x in 2023, and EBITDA less capital expenditure covered it 2.87x in 2025. Cash interest paid exceeded the income-statement interest expense by USD 49.6 million largely because the expense is shown net of interest income and capitalized interest.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_sealed-air-corp.htm.jsonl, pages 70, 112; calculation C30; calculation C40; calculation C46

- Liquidity at year-end was USD 1,344.0 million, cash of USD 344.0 million plus the undrawn USD 1,000.0 million revolver, which covers the USD 724.8 million of current debt 1.85x. The USD 600 million senior secured notes due October 2026 fell due before the as-of date; a USD 600 million delayed draw term loan was available to October 15, 2026, but whether it was drawn is not stated.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_sealed-air-corp.htm.jsonl, pages 84, 148–150; calculation C16; calculation C31; calculation C32

- Maturities are uneven rather than front-loaded: USD 626.4 million falls due in 2026, USD 445.9 million in 2027, USD 791.3 million in 2028, USD 452.1 million in 2029, USD 339.9 million in 2030 and USD 1,281.8 million after 2030, so 2028 is the largest of the five years to 2030. The October 2025 credit agreement moved the bank debt out to October 2030, replacing the March 2027 Term Loan A of USD 685.2 million at the end of 2024 with a Term Loan A due October 2030 of USD 371.6 million, and the sources do not say whether the acquisition left this structure in place.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_sealed-air-corp.htm.jsonl, pages 148–150

- The issuer's own leverage is lower than the reported-EBITDA measure because adjusted EBITDA of USD 1,134.3 million is USD 195.3 million above reported EBITDA, mainly restructuring and other charges and USD 41.1 million of share-based compensation: net debt over adjusted EBITDA is 3.23x against 3.90x, and the covenant measure of 2.95x sits against a 4.50x maximum.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_sealed-air-corp.htm.jsonl, pages 61, 85; EX-99.1_2025-12-31_see.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 11–12; calculation C42; calculation C27

- Debt-like funding sits outside the debt figure: USD 50.0 million of receivables sold under the U.S. securitization program started in December 2025 is not carried as debt and its cash is in operating cash flow, receivables factored in 2025 totalled USD 628.7 million against USD 721.7 million in 2024, supply chain finance obligations inside payables were USD 147.1 million against USD 161.1 million, and operating lease liabilities of USD 90.4 million are separate lines.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_sealed-air-corp.htm.jsonl, pages 83–85, 109, 142–146; calculation C33

- Subsequent events are kept out of the period figures: the February 2026 dividend and the merger that completed on April 9, 2026 are shown only in the post-balance-sheet table, and the sources give no acquisition financing, so net debt after closing is not established.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_sealed-air-corp.htm.jsonl, page 177; STATUS_15-12G_2026-04-20_see.htm.jsonl, page 1
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against a cautious reading is that the issuer's own measures are lower than the ones used here: covenant leverage was 2.95x against a 4.50x maximum, net leverage on adjusted EBITDA was 3.23x, and free cash flow after dividends was USD 339.3 million in 2025 and USD 389.8 million in 2024. The view would soften if post-closing statements show net debt close to the year-end figure, and it would harden if they show the acquisition financing added materially to it, which is the open question the sources cannot answer.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_sealed-air-corp.htm.jsonl, pages 61, 85, 111–112; calculation C13; calculation C14
### Limitations

- Every leverage, coverage and liquidity figure is struck at December 31, 2025 or earlier, so none of them describes the company after the merger completed; a conclusion about today's leverage needs post-closing statements the sources do not contain.

- EBITDA (Reported) is derived here from net earnings, interest, tax and depreciation and amortization because the issuer states only an adjusted figure; leverage on the issuer's measure is shown beside it, and the two differ by USD 195.3 million in 2025.
Basis: calculation C42

- The undrawn committed facilities figure of USD 1,000.0 million is the revolver the annual report states; the annual report's lines-of-credit table shows USD 1,197.0 million of unused lines and the results release about USD 1,060 million of unused committed lines, so undrawn committed capacity lies between USD 1,000.0 million and USD 1,197.0 million and the liquidity figure is a floor.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_sealed-air-corp.htm.jsonl, pages 84, 154; EX-99.1_2025-12-31_see.htm.jsonl, page 5; calculation C44
- Debt maturing after 2030 is one total in the filing, so the ladder chart stops at 2030 and USD 1,281.8 million sits in the reconciliation instead of a chart bar.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_sealed-air-corp.htm.jsonl, page 149; calculation C23

## Gaps

- No financial statements, results or trading update after December 31, 2025 are supplied, so leverage, interest cover, liquidity and every other figure here stop at that date; this restricts every conclusion about the credit today. Severity High. Action: obtain post-closing financial statements or lender reports for the company.

- The capital structure after the merger completed on April 9, 2026 is not stated: the debt commitment letter is mentioned without terms, so net debt after closing cannot be stated and year-end net debt of USD 3,665.7 million is the last figure available. Severity High. Action: obtain the financing documents or a post-closing debt schedule.

- The outcome for the 1.573% senior secured notes due October 2026 (USD 600 million) and for the USD 600 million delayed draw term loan available to October 15, 2026 is not stated, so year-end current debt and the 2026 maturity cannot be rolled forward. Severity Medium. Action: obtain the debt schedule at a date after October 2026.

- Undrawn committed facilities differ across sources for FY2025: USD 1,000 million of revolver in the annual report, about USD 1,060 million of unused committed lines in the results release, and USD 1,197.0 million of unused lines of which the committed share is not split; no letters of credit are stated. This restricts the liquidity chart for FY2025, FY2024 and FY2023. Severity Medium. Action: obtain the committed and uncommitted split by facility.

- The covenant leverage definition is not stated: the annual report calls the measure debt to EBITDA in one place and a net leverage ratio in the risk factors, and the covenant EBITDA definition is not given. This restricts any headroom conclusion for FY2025 and FY2024. Severity Medium. Action: obtain the credit agreement.

- Maturities after 2030 of USD 1,281.8 million are one total, so the maturity chart stops at 2030, and USD 5.0 million of the difference between scheduled principal and carrying value is not itemized. This restricts the year-by-year wall beyond 2030. Severity Medium. Action: obtain note-level principal and the lease schedule.

- Principal is not stated for the 4.000% 2027, 5.000% 2029 and 6.875% 2033 notes, and security and ranking are not described for them (USD 1,293.7 million at carrying value); outstanding principal, drawn amount, margin, floor and reference-rate spread are not stated for the Term Loan A, the revolver or the delayed draw term loan; the rate type is not stated for the notes whose filing gives only a rate. This restricts the debt stack, which omits those notes, and the cumulative leverage of unsecured debt. Severity Medium. Action: obtain the indentures and the credit agreement.

- The U.S. securitization program started in December 2025 derecognizes USD 50.0 million of receivables outside debt with cash in operating activities, which makes FY2025 total debt and operating cash flow not fully comparable with FY2024. This restricts year-on-year debt and cash flow comparisons by about USD 50.0 million. Severity Medium. Action: carry the program beside debt in later analysis.

- Several cash flow cells are printed as dashes in the filing and are carried as not supplied rather than zero: impairment of debt investment in FY2025 and FY2023, tax refunds and deposits in FY2025, businesses acquired in FY2025, and repurchases of common stock in FY2025 and FY2024. This restricts nothing material because the activity totals tie. Severity Low. Action: none unless a dash is shown to be a nil amount.

- The cash flow statement closes on cash, cash equivalents and restricted cash of USD 345.3 million while the balance sheet shows cash of USD 344.0 million, a restricted amount of USD 1.3 million; net debt uses the balance sheet figure. Severity Low. Action: none.

- Funds from operations is not stated by the issuer and the method gives no formula, so funds from operations to debt is not calculable for any period. This restricts one coverage measure only. Severity Low. Action: define an agreed funds from operations proxy if committee needs it.

- No interim statements are supplied beyond the fourth quarter 2025 three-month columns of the results release, so no last-twelve-months figure is constructed and the quarterly trend is not available. This restricts quarterly leverage analysis only. Severity Low. Action: none while the full-year figures stand.

- Interest income is netted within interest expense, net and is stated only inside the interest expense table, so gross interest cost is a calculation (USD 274.8 million for FY2025) and not a reported line. Severity Low. Action: none.

spans.text: # Business and governance for Sealed Air Corp/De (issuer-1012100), as of 2026-11-18
## Request

Sealed Air Corp/De (issuer-1012100), as of 2026-11-18, credit snapshot pathway. Scope: the transaction, ownership, business, operating model and governance facts in the four supplied filings, including sponsor behavior where the filings document any.
## Sources
| Source | Document | Document date | sha256 | Use |

| 10-K_2024-12-31_sealed-air-corp.htm.jsonl | Annual report on Form 10-K of Sealed Air Corporation for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2024 | 2025-02-26 | 809ce92ba2d431a3d4a9f1d37023edc761248a67a97cec7779c49c479e27027c | Prior-year business and governance facts, executive and ownership position in early 2025; comparison with the 2025 annual report. |

| 10-K_2025-12-31_sealed-air-corp.htm.jsonl | Annual report on Form 10-K of Sealed Air Corporation for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2025 | 2026-03-02 | 82c4c91d640b6a99e501ef92e9529bf167e6836d7c667123c1f99182de8c964f | Primary source: business, segments, merger terms, ownership table, governance, executive officers, capital allocation, legal matters. |

| EX-99.1_2025-12-31_see.htm.jsonl | Exhibit 99.1 results release for the fourth quarter and full year 2025 | 2026-03-02 | 8e659f869890926eac235f32c50d49018142a623ac38809e5149545764ee1ca1 | Management description of the acquisition (enterprise value, per-share price, expected closing) and year-end net debt statement. |

| STATUS_15-12G_2026-04-20_see.htm.jsonl | Form 15 certification and notice of termination of registration of Sealed Air Corporation | 2026-04-20 | 37dcda77f63552d032343b335621baa4af5e9e92a6f903f1d638b61d3f2822f9 | Completion date of the merger, post-closing ownership and end of public reporting. |
| Handoff | Module | sha256 |
| Source readiness | CP-0 | 73526f45cde93ce1074d268f33a8f50a70ffd84b055e9d5b799c5469c307641e |
## Findings
### Bottom line

Sealed Air is a diversified packaging supplier that changed hands on April 9, 2026, and for creditors the open question is the new owner's capital structure, which the sources do not disclose, rather than the business itself.
Basis: STATUS_15-12G_2026-04-20_see.htm.jsonl, page 1; Source readiness (CP-0)

The company has two segments, Food at 67.1% of 2025 net sales and Protective at 32.9%, and no customer above 10% of segment revenue, so customer concentration is low. The CD&R-affiliated buyer agreed a total purchase price of USD 10.3 billion, 9.08x FY2025 Adjusted EBITDA, funded in part by a debt commitment whose terms are not given. Public reporting ended on April 20, 2026, so later governance and financing facts are not established.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_sealed-air-corp.htm.jsonl, pages 7, 8, 14, 137; calculation C1
### Key findings

- The business is diversified but the mix is shifting toward Food: Food net sales rose by USD 75.0 million to USD 3,594.7 million between 2023 and 2025 at a 23.1% Adjusted EBITDA margin, while Protective fell by USD 204.1 million, or 10.36%, to USD 1,765.1 million at 17.6%. Food is the larger and higher-margin segment, so Protective softness matters less to creditors than it would if the segments were equal.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_sealed-air-corp.htm.jsonl, pages 77, 137; calculation C5; calculation C6; calculation C7; calculation C8

- Concentration is low by customer and moderate by channel: no customer or affiliated group exceeded 10% of segment revenue in 2025, and distributors sold about 60% of Protective sales, so the exposure sits with the distribution channel rather than any single account. 51.36% of net sales came from the U.S. and 49% from outside it.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_sealed-air-corp.htm.jsonl, pages 8, 13, 14, 139; calculation C9

- Margins depend on resin cost pass-through and volume: raw materials are about one-third of cost of sales, which is 70.21% of net sales, and in 2025 price was flat (USD -0.1 million) while volume fell USD 65.4 million, whereas in 2024 price fell USD 118.8 million and volume rose USD 34.7 million, so earnings are exposed to a repeat of 2024 pricing pressure.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_sealed-air-corp.htm.jsonl, pages 14, 66, 109; calculation C12

- The purchase price is high against earnings and its funding is undisclosed: USD 10.3 billion is 9.08x FY2025 Adjusted EBITDA and implies USD 6,211.6 million for the equity at the February 2026 share count, leaving USD 4,088.4 million that the sources do not allocate between assumed debt, refinanced debt and other items. The debt commitment letter is referred to without terms, so post-closing leverage, security and ranking are not established.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_sealed-air-corp.htm.jsonl, pages 7, 20, 233; EX-99.1_2025-12-31_see.htm.jsonl, page 1; calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C3

- Control moved from a widely held public shareholder base, where the largest holders had 10.9%, 10.1% and 9.2%, to a single owner, and public reporting ended with the Form 15; the annual report states no board, fee, distribution or financial-policy terms for the new owner, so creditor alignment under sponsor ownership is not established.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_sealed-air-corp.htm.jsonl, pages 234, 236; STATUS_15-12G_2026-04-20_see.htm.jsonl, page 1

- Senior leadership turned over heavily around the sale: the chief executive who started on July 1, 2024 left on February 12, 2025, 226 days later, and the chief financial officer succeeded him; the chief operating officer left on April 1, 2025, a new chief financial officer started on August 25, 2025 and the Food president changed on November 20 and December 8, 2025. This raises execution risk through the change of ownership but is not evidence of creditor-adverse conduct.
Basis: 10-K_2024-12-31_sealed-air-corp.htm.jsonl, pages 180, 186; 10-K_2025-12-31_sealed-air-corp.htm.jsonl, pages 52, 199–200, 203; calculation C11

- Pre-sale financial policy was creditor-aligned on the evidence: dividends held at USD 0.80 per share a year, USD 119.2 million paid in 2025, which is 18.98% of operating cash flow, no share repurchases are printed for 2024 or 2025, long-term debt repayments exceeded new long-term borrowing by USD 367.6 million in 2025, and the October 2025 credit agreement extended maturities to 2030, although it also loosened covenants to allow more debt.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_sealed-air-corp.htm.jsonl, pages 111–112, 150; calculation C13; calculation C15
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence for a more comfortable view is that the filings document no extraction, creditor-adverse transaction or distribution beyond the regular dividend, the customer base is diversified, and the buyer is described by management as an investor with industrial and packaging experience, which is a management characterization and not evidence of how it will treat creditors. The view would improve if the financing documents show a large equity contribution and no priming or disclosure restrictions, and it would worsen if they show debt-funded distributions or reduced reporting to creditors.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_sealed-air-corp.htm.jsonl, pages 7, 21, 150
### Limitations
- The acquisition financing is not described, so conclusions about post-closing leverage, security, ranking and the equity cheque are not established.

- Sponsor behavior can only be assessed from actions toward this issuer, and the filings document only the purchase, so the sponsor and governance risk level is not established, which is different from low.
- Governance facts for the board, officers and holders are as of early 2026 before closing; the post-closing board, management and creditor reporting are not established.
- Segment margins are the issuer's own Adjusted EBITDA measures, which exclude special items, so they are not comparable with reported operating profit.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_sealed-air-corp.htm.jsonl, page 77

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

On November 16, 2025 Sealed Air agreed to be acquired by Sword Purchaser, LLC, a Delaware company affiliated with CD&R, through the merger of Sword Merger Sub, Inc. into the company, for a total purchase price of USD 10.3 billion in cash and USD 42.15 per share. Stockholders adopted the agreement on February 25, 2026, the antitrust waiting period ended early on December 23, 2025, and the merger completed on April 9, 2026, 144 days after signing, leaving the company a wholly owned subsidiary of Parent. The annual report calls the figure a total purchase price and the results release calls it an enterprise value; both state USD 10.3 billion.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_sealed-air-corp.htm.jsonl, pages 7, 8, 19; EX-99.1_2025-12-31_see.htm.jsonl, page 1; STATUS_15-12G_2026-04-20_see.htm.jsonl, page 1; calculation C10

The financing of the acquisition is not described: the annual report names a Debt Commitment Letter and warns that Parent could fail to obtain the debt financing on its terms, but gives no amount, ranking, security or pricing, and no equity contribution is stated. A termination fee of USD 205.1 million, 1.99% of the purchase price, was payable by the company in stated circumstances. While the merger was pending the company could not issue securities, incur certain debt, declare certain dividends or make certain capital expenditures without Parent's approval.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_sealed-air-corp.htm.jsonl, pages 7, 20, 21; calculation C4

New debt before the acquisition was raised to buy Liquibox and to refinance shorter notes: a USD 650.0 million incremental term loan used on February 1, 2023 and USD 775.0 million of 6.125% notes due 2028 issued on January 31, 2023 funded Liquibox with cash on hand and repurchased the 4.500% notes due 2023, USD 425.0 million of 7.250% notes due 2031 on November 20, 2023 repurchased the 5.125% notes due 2024, and USD 400.0 million of 6.500% notes due 2032 on June 28, 2024 repurchased the 5.500% notes due 2025. On October 31, 2025 an amended and restated credit agreement extended maturities to October 2030, added a USD 600 million delayed draw term loan available to October 15, 2026 and relaxed certain covenants. No debt issued after December 31, 2025 is described in the sources.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_sealed-air-corp.htm.jsonl, pages 150–153

spans.text: # Fundamental credit for Sealed Air Corp/De (issuer-1012100), as of 2026-11-18
## Request

Sealed Air Corp/De (issuer-1012100), as of 2026-11-18, credit snapshot pathway. Scope: the integrated fundamental credit view from the four supplied filings and the three earlier analyses (source readiness, financial foundation, business and governance), covering cash-flow durability, liquidity and refinancing, the ownership change, a downside path, a materiality ranking and monitoring triggers.
## Sources
| Source | Document | Document date | sha256 | Use |

| 10-K_2024-12-31_sealed-air-corp.htm.jsonl | Annual report on Form 10-K of Sealed Air Corporation for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2024 | 2025-02-26 | 809ce92ba2d431a3d4a9f1d37023edc761248a67a97cec7779c49c479e27027c | Covenant leverage ratio at the end of 2024, used for the trend in covenant headroom. |

| 10-K_2025-12-31_sealed-air-corp.htm.jsonl | Annual report on Form 10-K of Sealed Air Corporation for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2025 | 2026-03-02 | 82c4c91d640b6a99e501ef92e9529bf167e6836d7c667123c1f99182de8c964f | Primary source: business and segments, price and volume bridge, segment gross profit, cash flow, liquidity and securitization notes, debt note, covenants, ratings, merger terms and risk factors. |

| EX-99.1_2025-12-31_see.htm.jsonl | Exhibit 99.1 results release for the fourth quarter and full year 2025 | 2026-03-02 | 8e659f869890926eac235f32c50d49018142a623ac38809e5149545764ee1ca1 | Fourth quarter 2025 segment results, the issuer's statement of available liquidity and net leverage, and its description of the acquisition. |

| STATUS_15-12G_2026-04-20_see.htm.jsonl | Form 15 certification and notice of termination of registration of Sealed Air Corporation | 2026-04-20 | 37dcda77f63552d032343b335621baa4af5e9e92a6f903f1d638b61d3f2822f9 | Merger completion date, one holder of record and the end of public reporting. |
| Handoff | Module | sha256 |
| Source readiness | CP-0 | 73526f45cde93ce1074d268f33a8f50a70ffd84b055e9d5b799c5469c307641e |
| Financial foundation | CP-1 | 2b4eef6cfb2d0a8b9a09bf393a9591d3e4e5e16a226e72ab7dd52d6441346246 |
| Business & governance | CP-1A | ca7e05d2224766a314375b782e2ba2bb4b76d1b8681160fa9ed8c14f07343812 |
## Findings
### Bottom line

Sealed Air was an adequate and deleveraging packaging credit at the end of 2025, but the April 2026 CD&R buyout makes that picture historical, so creditors cannot size post-closing leverage, ranking or reporting from the filings.
Basis: STATUS_15-12G_2026-04-20_see.htm.jsonl, page 1; Source readiness (CP-0)

The support is cash generation: debt fell by USD 394.2 million in 2025 (USD 344.2 million like-for-like), free cash flow after dividends was USD 339.3 million and the covenant leverage ratio of 2.95x sat inside its 4.50x maximum. The constraint is that reported EBITDA of USD 939.0 million was barely above the USD 926.1 million of 2023, USD 600 million of secured notes fell due in October 2026, and the buyer's USD 10.3 billion price is 9.08x FY2025 adjusted EBITDA with its financing undisclosed.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_sealed-air-corp.htm.jsonl, pages 7, 58, 85, 87, 142–143, 149; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C3; calculation C14; calculation C12; calculation C5; calculation C6; calculation C39
### Key findings

- Cash generation, not earnings growth, carried the improvement, so the deleveraging is dependable only while cash conversion holds. Free cash flow was USD 458.5 million in 2025, or USD 339.3 million after dividends, and total debt fell by USD 394.2 million, yet reported EBITDA, derived here from the statements because the issuer reports only an adjusted figure, was USD 939.0 million, only USD 12.9 million above the USD 926.1 million of 2023. The new U.S. receivables program flatters both measures by up to USD 50.0 million: its sale proceeds sit in operating cash flow and the USD 50.0 million of borrowings under its predecessor left reported debt, so like-for-like free cash flow lies between USD 408.5 million and USD 458.5 million and the like-for-like debt reduction was USD 344.2 million.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_sealed-air-corp.htm.jsonl, pages 58, 87, 89, 142–143; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C3; calculation C5; calculation C6; calculation C7; calculation C14; calculation C17

- Liquidity is adequate and larger than the earlier financial analysis could show, but it is thin in the United States and sensitive to ratings. Committed undrawn capacity is USD 1,055.3 million, the USD 1,000.0 million revolver (due in 2030) plus USD 55.3 million left in the two securitization programs, almost all of it in the U.S. program and both programs expiring annually, which matches the issuer's own statement of about USD 1.06 billion; with year-end cash of USD 344.0 million (pro forma cash after the February 2026 dividend, the merger and the October 2026 notes maturity is not established) liquidity is USD 1,399.3 million and covers the USD 724.8 million of current debt 1.93x. About 89% of that cash sits outside the United States, leaving roughly USD 38 million at home, and securitization availability can fall if ratings fall, which the agencies had put under review for downgrade.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_sealed-air-corp.htm.jsonl, pages 82, 83, 84, 86, 143–144, 150, 154; EX-99.1_2025-12-31_see.htm.jsonl, page 5; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C28; calculation C29; calculation C30; calculation C31; calculation C33

- Business quality is strong on scale and customer spread, but the Protective segment is eroding and Food carries the credit. No customer exceeded 10% of net sales and 49% of net sales came from outside the United States, and Food produced USD 829.1 million, or 73.09%, of USD 1,134.3 million of adjusted EBITDA. Protective net sales fell 10.36% between 2023 and 2025 and its gross profit fell 17.00%, or USD 103.2 million, taking its gross margin from 30.83% to 28.55% while Food's rose from 29.40% to 30.56%, which is operating deleverage in the weaker segment.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_sealed-air-corp.htm.jsonl, pages 8, 66, 68, 77; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C22; calculation C23; calculation C24; calculation C26; calculation C50

- Raw-material pass-through protects Food's margin but lags it, so the first months of a resin spike would squeeze earnings before prices catch up. Raw materials are about one-third of cost of sales, roughly USD 1,254.3 million on 2025 cost of sales, and about 45% of Food's sales reprice with raw-material indices about six months late; the filing describes formula pricing only for Food's North American and Asia-Pacific business. In 2024 consolidated price fell by USD 118.8 million, mainly on raw-material deflation and pricing pressure, so the same mechanism lowers reported sales when resin falls.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_sealed-air-corp.htm.jsonl, pages 14, 25, 56, 66, 67, 68; calculation C27

- The earnings gains came from cost take-out that has finished, which leaves fewer self-help levers for the next price or volume shock. The restructuring program that concluded in the third quarter of 2025 delivered its full USD 160 million annualized savings target, yet adjusted EBITDA rose only USD 27.7 million between 2023 and 2025 while net sales fell USD 129.1 million, so on a rough comparison about USD 132.3 million of the savings was absorbed by price, volume and other costs. Capital expenditure is planned at USD 225 million for 2026, USD 55.5 million or 32.74% above 2025, which lowers free cash flow by that amount if earnings are unchanged.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_sealed-air-corp.htm.jsonl, pages 61, 70, 82; calculation C18; calculation C19; calculation C20; calculation C44

- Refinancing risk is concentrated in 2026 to 2028, and the buyout has turned it from a market-access question into an open one. USD 1,863.6 million, or 47.33% of scheduled principal, falls due in those three years, including USD 600 million of secured notes in October 2026 and the largest single year, USD 791.3 million, in 2028; replacing the October 2026 notes at the coupon of the 2032 senior notes would add about USD 29.56 million of annual interest and lower EBITDA cover of cash interest from 3.50x to 3.15x, an illustration that holds other items constant. The October 2025 credit agreement moved bank maturities to October 2030 but makes a change in control an event of default, so the bank debt had to be repaid, amended or waived when the buyout closed, and whether that happened is not established.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_sealed-air-corp.htm.jsonl, pages 112, 149, 150, 151; calculation C13; calculation C34; calculation C35; calculation C36

- The buyout is the dominant credit event, and its financing decides whether the credit is better or worse than at year-end. The USD 10.3 billion total purchase price, which the results release calls an enterprise value, is 9.08x FY2025 adjusted EBITDA and implies USD 6,211.6 million for the equity, leaving USD 4,088.4 million, which is only USD 78.7 million above year-end total debt of USD 4,009.7 million, so the price looks consistent with repaying existing debt but says nothing about how much new debt funds the equity. Each USD 1,000.0 million of added net debt would add 0.88x to leverage on adjusted EBITDA. Year-end net debt was USD 3,665.7 million, or 3.90x reported EBITDA; pro forma for the estimated dividend declared on 2026-02-16 it was USD 3,695.2 million, or 3.94x, while pro forma for the merger completed on 2026-04-09 and for the October 2026 notes it is not established.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_sealed-air-corp.htm.jsonl, pages 7, 20, 177, 233; STATUS_15-12G_2026-04-20_see.htm.jsonl, page 1; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C1; calculation C4; calculation C8; calculation C9; calculation C10; calculation C39; calculation C40; calculation C41

- Creditor protections weakened before the sale and visibility ended after it. The October 2025 amendment adjusted covenants to allow more debt while the reported covenant ratio was 2.95x against a 4.50x maximum, a gap of 1.55x under a definition the filing does not set out, and the board still declared a USD 29.5 million dividend on 2026-02-16 during the pending merger. The Form 15 of 2026-04-20 ended public reporting, and the only sponsor action the filings document is the purchase, so sponsor behavior toward creditors, creditor reporting and the new board are not established.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_sealed-air-corp.htm.jsonl, pages 85, 150, 177; STATUS_15-12G_2026-04-20_see.htm.jsonl, page 1; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C9; calculation C12

- Funding outside reported debt adds a modest hidden burden. About USD 151 million of receivables would otherwise be outstanding because of customer financing programs and the off-balance-sheet U.S. securitization, and USD 147.1 million of payables are supplier-finance invoices, together USD 298.1 million, or 7.43% of total debt and 0.32x of reported EBITDA. Pension underfunding is small at USD 45.3 million, operating lease liabilities of USD 90.4 million and purchase commitments of USD 147.1 million sit outside total debt, the Diversey sale indemnities have no estimable maximum, and the one litigation matter the filing describes was settled on 2025-12-16 without material effect.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_sealed-air-corp.htm.jsonl, pages 84, 85, 109, 146, 163, 174, 175; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C42; calculation C43; calculation C54
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against a cautious reading is that the filings show a credit that was improving and conservatively run. Debt fell by USD 394.2 million in 2025, the covenant ratio of 2.95x was well inside its 4.50x limit, the revolver was undrawn, bank maturities had been moved to October 2030, and the senior secured debt was rated Baa2 and BBB-, investment grade at both agencies. Protective adjusted EBITDA also rose 21% in the fourth quarter, to USD 80 million from USD 67 million, which suggests the erosion may be bottoming, and management states that U.S. cash and committed facilities available to U.S. borrowers are sufficient for at least the next 12 months. A buyout can also leave existing creditors protected if sponsor equity is large, or end their exposure if the notes were repaid at closing. The view would improve if post-closing statements show leverage on the issuer's own measure no higher than its year-end level, the notes and credit agreement left in place and creditor reporting continuing. It would worsen if the financing adds net debt on a scale where each USD 1,000.0 million adds 0.88x, if the secured layer grows ahead of the unsecured notes, or if Protective volume resumes falling.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_sealed-air-corp.htm.jsonl, pages 58, 82, 84, 85, 86, 150; EX-99.1_2025-12-31_see.htm.jsonl, page 4; calculation C3; calculation C12; calculation C41; calculation C49; calculation C51
### Limitations

- The overall assessment of an adequate credit describes the company on December 31, 2025, and it would move up or down once the buyout financing, its security and its guarantees are known, because none of that is in the filings.

- EBITDA here is derived from the statements and sits USD 195.3 million below the issuer's adjusted figure, so the leverage and cover conclusions read weaker than the issuer's own leverage measure, and they soften if the issuer's add-backs are accepted.
Basis: calculation C5; calculation C11

- The committed liquidity of USD 1,055.3 million is this module's reconciliation of three notes that the issuer does not itemize, and the securitization part depends on eligible receivables and ratings, so the liquidity conclusion is lower if availability sits below the program limits.
Basis: calculation C28; calculation C29
- The like-for-like free cash flow range uses the year-end derecognized balance as the size of the 2025 benefit, so the cash conversion conclusion carries an uncertainty of up to USD 50.0 million.
Basis: calculation C17

- Segment gross profit excludes corporate cost and the segments' adjusted EBITDA is the issuer's own measure, so the conclusion that Protective is eroding while Food carries the credit could be overstated or understated if costs moved between segments.
- No peer set, market prices or agency commentary were supplied, so the comparison with other leveraged packaging issuers is a judgement and the view carries no market cross-check.

- The interest and EBITDA sensitivities are mechanical illustrations that assume refinancing at the coupon of the 2032 senior notes and hold everything else constant, so they show the scale of the effect on cover and not a forecast.
Basis: calculation C35; calculation C36; calculation C37
### Strengths and weaknesses

The main strengths before the sale were cash generation, scale with a spread of customers, and a debt structure that had been lengthened and reduced. Free cash flow after capital expenditure of USD 458.5 million supported a debt reduction of USD 394.2 million, no customer exceeded 10% of net sales, and the October 2025 amendment moved bank maturities to October 2030 while the secured debt carried investment-grade ratings.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_sealed-air-corp.htm.jsonl, pages 8, 58, 86, 87, 150; calculation C3; calculation C14

The main weaknesses are a shrinking Protective segment, earnings held up by savings that have now ended, USD 1,863.6 million of maturities in 2026 to 2028, and an ownership change that leaves post-closing leverage, ranking and reporting unknown. Each pushes the creditor toward the same conclusion: the year-end credit was adequate, and what it is today depends on documents that are not available.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_sealed-air-corp.htm.jsonl, pages 20, 70, 149; calculation C20; calculation C24; calculation C34

On the nine dimensions of the financial profile, scale and market position is Strong, because net sales of USD 5,359.8 million are sold in 119 countries and territories, and business diversification is Strong, because no customer exceeds 10% of net sales. Competitive advantage is Average, because the filing gives no market share, says it generally imposes no annual minimum purchase volumes on distributors and shows contracted remaining performance obligations of only USD 17.9 million. Cost and capex flexibility is Average, because capital expenditure fell from USD 244.2 million in 2023 to USD 169.5 million in 2025 but the savings program is finished and raw materials are about one-third of cost of sales. Margin stability is Average, because adjusted EBITDA margin rose from 20.2% to 21.2% through cost take-out while price fell by USD 118.8 million in 2024. Free cash flow stability is Average, because free cash flow was USD 272.0 million in 2023 after USD 195.0 million of tax deposits and USD 458.5 million in 2025. Ability to refinance and access capital markets is Average before the sale and Not Assessable after it. Liquidity position is Average, because liquidity of USD 1,399.3 million covers current debt 1.93x but is thin in the United States. Financial policy and governance is Average before the sale, on the evidence of debt repayment and no repurchases in 2024 and 2025, and Not Assessable after closing.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_sealed-air-corp.htm.jsonl, pages 8, 14, 61, 66, 87, 88, 89, 132; calculation C14; calculation C21; calculation C30; calculation C31; calculation C44; calculation C48; calculation C50
### Company description and ownership

Sealed Air Corporation, a Delaware company, is the registrant of a consolidated group that sells packaging materials, automation equipment and services to food processors (Food, 67.1% of 2025 net sales) and to e-commerce, logistics, industrial and medical customers (Protective, 32.9%). The business model builds cash-flow visibility through long customer relationships, equipment placed with customers and brands, but not through contracts: remaining performance obligations were USD 17.9 million against net sales of USD 5,359.8 million, and the filing says it generally imposes no annual minimum purchase volumes on distributors, who handle about 60% of Protective sales. Debt service therefore rests on repeat purchasing and the spread of customers rather than contracted backlog, which gives refinancing lenders little revenue visibility beyond the current order flow.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_sealed-air-corp.htm.jsonl, pages 6, 8, 14, 132, 133; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C48; calculation C50

### Revenue, cost and cash conversion

Revenue is stable rather than growing and its quality differs by segment. Net sales fell 0.61% in 2025 and 2.35% between 2023 and 2025; Food price rose by USD 21.5 million in 2025 on contract-formula pricing while its volume fell by USD 25.4 million, and Protective lost USD 40.0 million of volume from earlier customer churn in its fulfillment portfolio and USD 21.6 million of price. The credit implication is that Food's formula pricing keeps its margin more predictable, while Protective's price and volume are exposed to the e-commerce and industrial cycle and to distributor purchasing that carries no minimum commitments.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_sealed-air-corp.htm.jsonl, pages 14, 66, 67; calculation C18

Margins can be defended against modest volume pressure but not against a repeat of the 2024 Protective shock without further cost action. Gross margin was 29.8% in 2025, cost of sales is 70.2% of net sales, and in 2024 an 8.08% fall in Protective net sales cut its adjusted EBITDA by 13.35%, or USD 48.3 million, even with savings flowing in. The plant network and workforce are largely fixed cost, so volume losses weigh heavily on margin, and the finished savings program removes the offset that held 2025 earnings flat.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_sealed-air-corp.htm.jsonl, pages 10, 65, 68, 77, 79; calculation C25

Cash conversion is moderate and flattered at the margin. Free cash flow was 48.83% of reported EBITDA in 2025, dividends took 18.98% of operating cash flow, and capital expenditure of 3.16% of net sales gives some flexibility, since it fell USD 74.7 million between 2023 and 2025, but 2026 spending is planned higher. The issuer expects USD 201 million of interest and about USD 155 million of tax payments in 2026, plus pension contributions of about USD 10 million and benefit payments of about USD 9 million, so interest and taxes together, USD 356 million, call on more cash than the USD 225 million of planned capital expenditure.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_sealed-air-corp.htm.jsonl, pages 79, 80, 81, 82, 87; calculation C15; calculation C16; calculation C44; calculation C47
### Competitive forces and external factors

Competitive rivalry is the force that matters most for credit and it is uneven. The filing describes global and regional competitors competing on performance, automation, sustainability, service and price, with competitors and customers consolidating, and Protective has lost both price and volume since 2023, which is evidence that rivalry caps its pricing; Food, with equipment-integrated materials sold directly to food processors, shows rising margins. For creditors this means Protective earnings are the first to give way and Food holds the cash flow.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_sealed-air-corp.htm.jsonl, pages 14, 27, 56, 57, 66; calculation C23; calculation C24

The threat of new entrants is moderate, because brands, equipment integration, product registration requirements and plant scale are barriers but the filing says the business does not depend on any single patent or trademark. The threat of substitutes comes from paper, molded pulp and corrugated alternatives in protective packaging and from regulation of plastics and PFAS, which could cut demand or force reformulation; Food's shelf-life and food-safety function makes switching harder, although competing food packaging also uses plastic, metals and other materials. Buyer power is limited by customer spread, with no customer above 10%, but is real in Protective, where distributors carry no minimum purchases, and supplier power is limited because most resins are available from several sources, although sole-source suppliers exist in some regions and a resin spike reaches cost of sales ahead of prices.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_sealed-air-corp.htm.jsonl, pages 9, 13, 14, 15, 16, 25, 36, 37; calculation C50

Regulation, trade policy and currency are material to credit and are treated here as the political, economic, social and technological factors that change cash flow. Plastic-waste legislation, PFAS rules and tariffs imposed during 2025 raise compliance cost, can lower demand for plastic packaging and complicate sourcing; 49% of net sales are earned outside the United States, so currency moves translate into reported earnings and a USD 15.1 million loss from highly inflationary economies, which the filing ties to Argentina, was treated as a special item in 2025; about USD 30 million of cash sits in Russia and Ukraine; sustainability preferences push customers toward recyclable materials; and labor agreements covering 31% of the roughly 5,200 covered employees expire in 2026. Automation demand from labor scarcity is a management claim that supports Food and Protective growth but is not quantified.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_sealed-air-corp.htm.jsonl, pages 8, 10, 12, 36, 37, 41, 61, 82; calculation C33; calculation C50
### Credit-translated SWOT

Strengths: cash generation of USD 458.5 million of free cash flow in 2025, funding debt reduction; a customer base with no account above 10%; the larger and higher-margin Food segment at 23.1% adjusted EBITDA margin; bank maturities extended to October 2030 with the revolver undrawn; and senior secured ratings in the investment-grade range.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_sealed-air-corp.htm.jsonl, pages 8, 77, 84, 86, 87, 150; calculation C14; calculation C26

Weaknesses: a Protective segment whose gross profit fell 17.00% in two years; revenue visibility of only USD 17.9 million of contracted obligations; raw materials at about one-third of cost of sales with pricing lag; USD 1,863.6 million of 2026 to 2028 maturities; and covenant changes that allow more debt.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_sealed-air-corp.htm.jsonl, pages 14, 25, 132, 149, 150; calculation C22; calculation C34; calculation C48

Opportunities: Food automation demand; lower interest cost after the 2025 debt repayments; and a sponsor that could supply equity or longer-dated funding, which the filings neither document nor rule out. Threats: acquisition debt that raises leverage and changes priority; the loss of public reporting; plastics regulation; tariffs; and distributor and e-commerce churn.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_sealed-air-corp.htm.jsonl, pages 12, 20, 36, 37, 67; STATUS_15-12G_2026-04-20_see.htm.jsonl, page 1
### Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds

The next 12 to 24 months are set by the buyout financing more than by operations. The operating tailwinds are the annualized savings already delivered, a Protective segment whose fourth-quarter volume rose by USD 6 million and whose adjusted EBITDA rose 21%, and Food contract-formula pricing; the headwinds are volume weakness in Food's industrial portfolio, raw-material deflation that lowers price, a USD 55.5 million step-up in capital expenditure, labor negotiations and the October 2026 notes. These support a stable operating outlook but cannot offset an unknown capital structure.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_sealed-air-corp.htm.jsonl, pages 10, 58, 66, 70, 82; EX-99.1_2025-12-31_see.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 4; calculation C44; calculation C49

Over three to five years the credit depends on regulation of plastics and PFAS, the success of sustainable products, customer consolidation in food processing and e-commerce, and the sponsor's financial policy. Management says Food is aligned with automation, labor scarcity and sustainability trends, a claim that favors Food but is not quantified; the sponsor's exit horizon, dividends and refinancing choices are not described.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_sealed-air-corp.htm.jsonl, pages 12, 27, 28, 36
### Downside scenario

The realistic downside combines a second Protective shock with leverage added by the buyout. The initiating condition is a repeat of 2024, when Protective volume fell USD 101.8 million and price USD 49.3 million, now joined by the weakness already seen in Food's industrial portfolio. The first operational break is distributor and fulfillment volume, which carries no minimum commitments, with price concessions on top; the financial transmission is that a repeat of the 13.35% fall in Protective adjusted EBITDA would cost USD 41.44 million, 3.65% of consolidated adjusted EBITDA, and lower EBITDA cover of cash interest from 3.50x to 3.34x, so the operating shock alone is survivable.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_sealed-air-corp.htm.jsonl, pages 66, 67, 77; calculation C13; calculation C25; calculation C45

What would turn it into a liquidity event is the capital structure behind the shock. Each USD 100.0 million of lost reported EBITDA lowers cover of cash interest to 3.12x, each USD 1,000.0 million of acquisition debt adds 0.88x to leverage on adjusted EBITDA, and replacing the October 2026 notes at the 2032 notes' coupon adds USD 29.56 million of interest, while securitization availability shrinks if ratings fall and the revolver is the only large committed source. Management levers are capital expenditure, which fell by USD 74.7 million between 2023 and 2025, the dividend, whose post-closing policy is unknown, and working-capital programs that are already large. Before the buyout resilience was sufficient to avoid liquidity distress, with cover of current debt 1.93x; after it, resilience is not established. The observable triggers are Protective volume, revolver drawings and any amendment or waiver of the credit agreement.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_sealed-air-corp.htm.jsonl, pages 82, 83, 84, 143, 149, 150; calculation C31; calculation C35; calculation C37; calculation C41; calculation C44
### Overall credit view

Overall, Sealed Air presented an adequate business profile at the end of 2025, supported by a USD 5,359.8 million sales base with no customer above 10%, a larger and higher-margin Food segment and conservative pre-sale financial policy, but credit quality is constrained by a Protective segment that lost 17.00% of gross profit in two years, finished cost savings and the loss of visibility after the CD&R buyout. Cash-flow durability appears adequate, because free cash flow was USD 458.5 million and USD 339.3 million after dividends, although up to USD 50.0 million of 2025 operating cash flow came from selling receivables that the old program had carried as debt. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on how the acquisition was financed and whether the October 2026 notes and the bank debt were repaid, amended or waived. The primary downside path is acquisition debt that raises leverage and interest cost while Protective volume stays weak. Further analysis would require the financing documents, a post-closing debt schedule, 2026 interim statements and creditor reporting terms. Fundamental credit assessment completed. Top risk: undisclosed acquisition financing and its effect on leverage, ranking and liquidity.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_sealed-air-corp.htm.jsonl, pages 20, 70, 87, 109, 149, 150; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C14; calculation C17; calculation C22
